The '''Empire of Khalindar''' is an imperial state whose twentieth-century history was shaped by the [[Avant Great War]], the failed postwar settlement promised at the [[Solaran-Khalindarian Conference of 1940]], and the [[Solara-Khalindar War]].

Old source material also uses the forms '''Khalindarian Empire''' and '''Khalindar Empire'''. This draft uses ''Empire of Khalindar'' as the clean AGGSWorld title.

This page is a 1940-1994 bridge draft, not a full founding history of the empire.

== Great War Position ==

Khalindar entered the anti-Vesperan war effort after Solara promised territorial gains, economic access, infrastructure development, military aid, and recognition. Khalindarian leaders saw the agreement as a binding wartime bargain rather than a symbolic diplomatic gesture.

Khalindar's wartime contribution helped pressure the [[Vesperan Empire]], but the full postwar settlement was not delivered after the Vesperan collapse in 1949. That failure became the basis of the [[Khalindarian reparations dispute]].

== Government And Society ==

By the late twentieth century, Khalindar was ruled through the emperor and the [[Imperial Council]], a ministerial state body rather than a royal court. The state was more centralized and restrictive than [[Solara]], with censorship, strong internal security, and limited political pluralism.

The country should not be written as socially disloyal or internally fractured during the Solara-Khalindar War. Khalindar's home front remained unified despite severe economic strain. The war effort was framed as endurance, sacrifice, and loyalty to the empire's historic claims.

== Military Character ==

Khalindar had large manpower reserves, strong strategic planning habits, and a leadership willing to absorb heavy costs. It was not uniformly high-tech. Much of its bomber force was old, including prop-driven aircraft, and the Albroke strike relied on range workarounds, sabotage, mines, submarines, fast craft, and one-way anti-carrier attacks.

The state also used proxy and deniable tools. Old source material connects [[Asgard Private Military Corporation]] to [[Emperor Mikael Khalindar IV]] in 1986 as a force designed to serve Khalindarian interests.

== Road To War ==

For decades after 1949, Khalindar repeatedly demanded enforcement of the promised settlement. Solara dismissed or minimized those demands, reinforcing Khalindarian claims that the empire had been exploited during the Great War.

Under Mikael IV, the reparations dispute became fused with imperial ambition, military preparation, and resentment of Solara's wealth. Khalindar chose war after renewed demands failed, opening the conflict with the attack on [[Albroke]] in March 1990.

== 1994 Position ==

By late 1994, Khalindar had failed to force a decisive victory over Solara, but it had also endured years of costly war without home-front collapse. The conflict moved toward mediation through the newly formed [[Avant Garde Global Peace Initiative]], setting up the January 1995 ceasefire and later postwar disputes.
